headline: Planning a Father-in-Law Suite: What to Review Before Hiring a Builder
articleBody:
Planning a secondary living addition involves more than picking paint colors and accessible fixtures. Before hiring a remodeling contractor or signing an addition agreement, make sure you address these vital design and zoning items.

Questions to Ask Before You Decide
First, determine how your municipality classifies the planned structure. An attached room addition has different code requirements than an independent accessory dwelling unit with full cooking capabilities. Ask potential builders about their experience handling local building permits, setback restrictions, and utility capacity assessments in your specific neighborhood. You should also confirm whether your existing electrical panel and water supply lines can handle additional everyday demand without costly service upgrades.

Next, focus on daily living accessibility. Incorporating zero-threshold showers, wider doorways, and slip-resistant flooring early in the design prevents costly structural modifications down the road. It is just as important to review how your builder manages trade coordination—such as drywall finishing, plumbing rough-ins, and exterior integration—so the new space matches your existing home's architectural style seamlessly.
